title: [Peek] Incorrect window/content scaling when re-triggering Peek on a different display
author: daverayment
summary: Peek mixes the activation Explorer monitor with the existing Peek window or foreground monitor during cross-display re-trigger, producing stale window or image scaling.

status.label: Implementation design ready
status.detail: Use one captured activation monitor source for unpinned scaling, sizing, and centering while preserving pinned behavior.

next_action.label: Review Peek cross-display sizing design
next_action.reason: The design is supported by deterministic repro and current code but needs approval before implementation.

judgment.rationale: The deterministic mixed-DPI repro aligns with a specific current-code mismatch: activation captures an Explorer HWND, while later scaling and preview sizing use the Peek or foreground window. The existing adversarial review found no blocking objection; mixed-DPI hardware remains the main verification dependency.
evidence: The report reproduces by opening Peek on one display, moving it to a differently scaled display, selecting another item on the first display, and triggering Peek again.
MainWindow activation captures the foreground Explorer HWND before activation.
MainWindow.Initialize currently derives ScalingFactor from the Peek window monitor.
FilePreviewer_PreviewSizeChanged calls GetForegroundWindow at asynchronous event time.
ImagePreviewer.UpdateMaxImageSize converts image pixels using ScalingFactor.
Related Peek issues cover separate minimum-size and native-image sizing scopes.
The existing design review recorded no blocking objections.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve the fork-side design to carry one activation placement HWND through unpinned scaling, sizing, and centering, with explicit fallback and pinned/CLI preservation.

fix_assessment.rationale: No implementation PR covers the issue; the existing fork-side design is a concrete repository fix with strong code and repro evidence.

proposed_fixes.title: Carry the activation monitor through Peek re-trigger sizing
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Peek captures the source Explorer HWND but later computes scale and preview sizing from the current Peek or foreground window, so a cross-display re-trigger can combine metrics from different DPI contexts.
plan: In src/modules/peek/Peek.UI/PeekXAML/MainWindow.xaml.cs, resolve and store one placement HWND per activation: the captured Explorer HWND for unpinned Explorer activation, otherwise the Peek HWND for pinned or CLI activation.

Set ViewModel.ScalingFactor from that placement HWND and use the same handle for monitor size, scale, and centering in FilePreviewer_PreviewSizeChanged instead of calling GetForegroundWindow asynchronously.
Reset or replace the stored handle at activation boundaries, fall back explicitly if Explorer closes, and preserve pinned behavior and CLI activation.
Keep FilePreview.ScalingFactor and ImagePreviewer.UpdateMaxImageSize as the existing propagation mechanism; only correct their monitor source and ordering.
Add guarded mixed-DPI UI coverage for window center and image bounds, skipping environments without distinct monitor DPI.
verification: Build the existing Peek project or solution through the repository's x64 Debug build workflow.
Run the existing Peek UI tests and the new mixed-DPI test where supported.

Use a 125% primary and 175% secondary display: open Peek on the primary, move it to the secondary, select another item on the primary, trigger Peek, and confirm window and image sizing use the primary display.
Repeat with a pinned window and CLI activation to confirm their placement semantics are unchanged.

confidence.rationale: The deterministic repro, exact monitor-source mismatch in current code, and prior independent adversarial review strongly support the fix; only hardware validation remains.

issue_context.summary: Peek reopens at the wrong size after moving between displays with different scaling and triggering it again from the original display.
known_information: The reporter provides deterministic steps and screenshots.
The primary display is 125% and the secondary is 175%.
Current MainWindow activation captures an Explorer HWND.
Current initialization and preview-size paths use other monitor sources.
Related issues 50243 and 50244 are separate minimum-size and native-image scopes.
A fork design exists and is awaiting approval.
inferences: The stale monitor source causes the incorrect window and image scale.
Pinned and CLI activation require separate fallback semantics.
Correcting the monitor source may not resolve the neighboring minimum-size/native-image issues.
issue_context.analysis: The reported sequence deliberately creates disagreement between the old Peek location and the new Explorer activation monitor. Current code has two timing-dependent monitor lookups, so a single per-activation source is a direct, testable correction.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue, automated triage, screenshots, labels, and related issue context.
Inspected MainWindow activation, initialization, preview-size, monitor helper, FilePreview scaling, and ImagePreviewer sizing paths.
Reviewed recent Peek history and performed an independent adversarial design pass covering pinned, CLI, fallback, ordering, and neighboring issues.

design.root_cause: The captured Explorer HWND is discarded after item selection; MainWindow.Initialize derives scale from the current Peek monitor and FilePreviewer_PreviewSizeChanged derives bounds and scale from a timing-dependent foreground HWND. Cross-display re-trigger therefore mixes DPI sources.
evidence: App.OnShowPeek captures the foreground Explorer HWND before activation.
MainWindow.Initialize calls GetMonitorScale on the Peek window.
FilePreviewer_PreviewSizeChanged calls GetForegroundWindow, GetMonitorSize, GetMonitorScale, and CenterOnMonitor.
ImagePreviewer.UpdateMaxImageSize divides image dimensions by ScalingFactor.

affected_files.purpose: Owns activation, monitor selection, scaling, sizing, centering, and uninitialization.
Carries the Explorer HWND captured before Peek activation.
Propagates item and scaling changes to previewers.
Converts image pixels using the current scaling factor.
Existing UI-test surface for Peek preview behavior.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Activation selection is available, but later scale and size calculations consult the current Peek or foreground window.
implementation_steps.change: Store a per-activation placement HWND, use it for scaling, monitor bounds, and centering, and fall back to the Peek HWND when the source handle is unavailable.
implementation_steps.code_block: private HWND _placementHwnd; _placementHwnd = !Pinned && selectedItem is SelectedItemByWindowHandle x && x.WindowHandle != HWND.Null ? x.WindowHandle : new HWND(GetWindowHandle()); ViewModel.ScalingFactor = _placementHwnd.GetMonitorScale(); // PreviewSizeChanged uses the same handle
edge_cases: Do not recenter or rescale pinned Peek.
Keep CLI activation on the Peek HWND.
Handle an Explorer HWND that becomes invalid before asynchronous preview completion.
tests: Unit-test the resolver for Explorer, pinned, CLI, null, and invalid-handle cases.
Run mixed-DPI UI coverage with image and non-image previews.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Scaling changes trigger preview-size recalculation and update image previewer state.
implementation_steps.change: Retain the existing propagation but ensure MainWindow sets the activation scale before preview-size completion; explicitly refresh only if event ordering proves insufficient.
implementation_steps.code_block: MainWindow sets ViewModel.ScalingFactor from placement HWND; existing FilePreview property change updates ImagePreviewer.UpdateMaxImageSize.
edge_cases: Avoid introducing a second scale source.
Preserve existing effective-pixel semantics for non-image previews.
tests: Assert image content bounds use the activation display scale.

verify: Build the existing Peek x64 Debug target.
Run filtered Peek UI tests where supported.
Execute the two-monitor 125%/175% reproduction and verify correct center, window size, and image bounds.
risks: A captured HWND can become invalid before async completion.
Changing placement selection can affect navigation, pinned windows, or CLI activation if scoping is wrong.
alternatives: Always use current foreground: rejected because async timing is the defect.
Always use Peek HWND: rejected because it preserves stale monitor placement after dragging.
Use only XamlRoot scale: rejected because it describes current location, not requested activation target.
